newsitem.title: VIETNAM: South Korea's President Kim to visit Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: South Korea's President Kim to visit Vietnam.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam has accepted an invitation to visit Vietnam, a Foreign Ministry spokesman in Hanoi said on Wednesday.
The spokesman said details of the visit were still being arranged by diplomats, but the Tuoi Tre newspaper said it was scheduled for late November.
Vietnam's Communist Party chief Do Muoi met Kim last year during a visit to South Korea aimed at boosting economic ties.
Since Vietnam and South Korea normalised relations in 1992, trade has increased rapidly. It soared to about $1.5 billion in 1995 from $493 million in 1992, Trade Ministry figures show.
South Korea is the fourth biggest foreign investor in Vietnam, with some $2.0 billion earmarked for 160 projects.
Seoul and Hanoi had severed diplomatic relations in 1975 after North Vietnam's communist forces defeated the U.S.-backed Saigon government, which South Korea supported.
